title: Causal world models under physical parameter shifts
abstract: arXiv:2610.29088v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: World models predict how embodied systems evolve under actions, but their accuracy can degrade when physical conditions move outside the training distribution. We study two components of causal modeling: which inputs a predictor may use, and how its mechanism computes their effects. In a synthetic benchmark with shortcut features, a frozen dependency mask derived from paired interventions reduces mean out-of-distribution (OOD) RMSE from 1.769 for a fully connected predictor to 0.697, close to the generator-oracle mask (0.694). For robot link-mass extrapolation in CausalWorld, with disjoint training and test mass ranges, we develop finger-local world models in which link masses enter inertia and dynamics-bias terms through explicit affine coefficients, actions act through either a learned torque network or the known PD controller, and learned residuals capture contact-related effects. translated_title: 物理参数偏移下的因果世界模型
translated_abstract: 世界模型用于预测具身系统在动作作用下如何演化，但当物理条件超出训练分布时，其准确性可能下降。我们研究了因果建模的两个组成部分：预测器可以使用哪些输入，以及其机制如何计算这些输入的影响。在一个带有捷径特征的合成基准测试中，通过成对干预导出的冻结依赖掩码，将全连接预测器的平均分布外（OOD）RMSE从1.769降至0.697，接近生成器预言掩码的0.694。针对CausalWorld中的机器人连杆质量外推任务（训练与测试的质量范围互不重叠），我们开发了手指局部世界模型：连杆质量通过显式仿射系数进入惯性和动力学偏置项，动作通过学习到的扭矩网络或已知的PD控制器施加作用，并通过学习到的残差来捕捉与接触相关的效应。（注：摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文将因果建模的两个关键组件——由成对干预导出的依赖掩码和显式的物理参数化机制——融入世界模型，使机器人在连杆质量等物理参数超出训练分布时仍能保持接近预言水平的准确预测。
en_tdlr: This paper integrates causal modeling components—intervention-derived dependency masks and explicit physical parameterizations—into world models, enabling near-oracle out-of-distribution prediction when physical parameters like robot link masses shift beyond the training range.
